exercise: Produce keyed records and explain each topic/partition/offset tuple.
interview_questions: How does a log differ from a queue?
Is offset 42 a global event ID?
answer_criteria: Identify offsets with topic and partition
failure_trap: Consumption is not deletion and offsets need not be dense.

exercise: Compare uniform and skewed warehouse/device key distributions.
interview_questions: Why select device versus warehouse as key?
failure_trap: More partitions do not resolve one indivisible hot key.

exercise: In a later three-broker profile record write acceptance after losing one then two replicas.
interview_questions: Does acks=all mean every configured replica?
What does RF=3/minimum ISR=2 trade off?
failure_trap: Acknowledgement settings do not prove unconditional durability.

exercise: Contrast single-node restart with a three-controller quorum failure.
interview_questions: Can metadata quorum restore a lost sole data copy?
failure_trap: A single broker restart does not prove replicated failover.

exercise: Compare client transport retry with application resubmission of the same event.
interview_questions: Why can an API retry still append another record?
failure_trap: Producer idempotence is not external business exactly-once.

exercise: Implement a later Kafka-to-Kafka branch committing output and consumed offsets together.
interview_questions: What belongs inside a Kafka transaction?
Why fence a previous producer incarnation?
failure_trap: Kafka transactions do not include arbitrary JDBC or HTTP effects.

exercise: Measure fixed-workload throughput and p95 latency at several batching configurations.
interview_questions: Why can batching improve latency under load?
failure_trap: An asynchronous send returning is not broker acknowledgement.

exercise: Run two groups over three partitions and record separate consumption.
interview_questions: Why do two groups both receive a record?
Why can some consumers remain idle?
answer_criteria: Bound classic active owners by partition count
failure_trap: Five classic consumers cannot independently own one partition at once.

exercise: Delay processing beyond the configured poll budget and save reassignment/error evidence.
interview_questions: Can healthy heartbeats coexist with poll timeout?
failure_trap: Do not copy Java/classic settings onto every Python/new-protocol client.

exercise: Restart before and after checkpointing next offset 8.
interview_questions: After processing record 7 what is committed?
Does earliest override a valid checkpoint?
failure_trap: The last processed offset itself is not the next recovery offset.

exercise: Complete offsets 10 and 12 while 11 fails and assert checkpoint cannot pass 11.
interview_questions: How do two partitions advance independently?
answer_criteria: Explicitly define quarantine as terminal policy
failure_trap: Maximum completed offset can skip unfinished work.

exercise: Revoke ownership during a DB task and verify recovery and deduplication.
interview_questions: Can the previous worker still mutate the database?
failure_trap: Group commit fencing does not itself fence external DB effects.

exercise: Check actual client support before comparing protocol behavior.
interview_questions: How does cooperative assignment reduce disruption?
Is consumer protocol identical to CooperativeStickyAssignor?
failure_trap: An assignment strategy is not the whole group protocol.

exercise: Compare restart rebalance counts under dynamic and static membership.
failure_trap: Static membership does not eliminate every rebalance.

exercise: Parallelize partitions while serializing each required ordering domain.
interview_questions: Why not share Java KafkaConsumer between arbitrary threads?
failure_trap: One global max offset is unsafe with parallel workers.

exercise: Route invalid schema and temporary DB outage differently.
interview_questions: What order changes when using retry topics?
failure_trap: Skipping every exception loses records and retrying invalid data forever stalls progress.

exercise: Crash before and after durable quarantine publication and source checkpoint.
interview_questions: Does redrive require a new event ID?
answer_criteria: Advance only after durable terminal decision
failure_trap: A failed DLQ write cannot justify skipping source data.

exercise: Check outage, replay, DLQ redrive and marker lifetimes against each other.
interview_questions: Are records retained until every consumer reads?
What if recovery offset was deleted?
failure_trap: Kafka retention is not a permanent archive.

exercise: Compare immutable event topic with compacted current-device-state topic.
failure_trap: Compaction cannot preserve guaranteed full event history.

exercise: Test added optional field and removed required field against old consumers.
interview_questions: Why place schema version in an envelope?
failure_trap: JSON syntax validity is not schema or semantic compatibility.

topic: Lag, event age and durable progress
exercise: Stall one hot partition and demonstrate misleading group averages.
interview_questions: Can lag be zero while effects failed?
Which signals distinguish CPU and sink delay?
failure_trap: Committed offsets alone do not prove correct effects.

exercise: Compare consumers while one producer transaction remains open.
interview_questions: Why can read_committed trail log end?
answer_criteria: Separate committed visibility and log end
failure_trap: Consumer isolation does not atomically include PostgreSQL.

exercise: Predict retained records under clean and explicitly unsafe election assumptions.
interview_questions: Why may a leader append not be visible?
failure_trap: A leader-local append is not a replicated durability guarantee.

exercise: Pause saturated partitions while maintaining required polling.
interview_questions: Why pause rather than sleep for minutes?
How do you choose queue capacity?
failure_trap: Unbounded application queues defeat broker buffering benefits.

exercise: Give relay, processor and observer narrowly scoped privileges.
interview_questions: What permission differs between consumer and producer?
failure_trap: Plaintext localhost success proves no production security claim.

exercise: Compare polling outbox with a CDC design and its operational obligations.
interview_questions: What happens when a replication slot stops draining?
failure_trap: Connector semantics vary and do not automatically remove duplicates.

exercise: Design an optional Streams metadata-join branch separate from baseline Python processing.
interview_questions: How do stream-table and stream-stream joins differ?
failure_trap: A plain consumer loop does not inherit Streams state or transaction guarantees.

exercise: Run duplicates, disconnects and rebalance scenarios and preserve config/runtime evidence.
interview_questions: What does one successful crash test establish?
failure_trap: A passing demonstration is not proof over every schedule.

exercise: Size from measured per-partition service rates then test skew and recovery.
interview_questions: Can more partitions fix one hot key?
How much spare capacity allows catch-up?
failure_trap: Partition count is not a universal throughput setting.

exercise: Crash between DB effect commit and source checkpoint and inspect one effect under replay.
failure_trap: Conflict UPDATE increments and premature marker deletion break deduplication.

exercise: Define an optional second-cluster exercise and allowed loss before implementing it.
interview_questions: Does local replication prove regional recovery?
How are source and target offsets related?
failure_trap: Colocated replicas do not prove multi-region resilience.

exercise: Document actual Python/Java clients before enabling protocol or transaction features.
interview_questions: Can Java properties be copied into Python?
Why state protocol/version in an answer?
failure_trap: Documented Kafka 4.x behavior may not fit the existing client.

exercise: Model warehouse/device/event/anomaly facts and one duplicated-attribute anomaly.
interview_questions: Why separate device metadata from events?
failure_trap: An ID column alone does not establish normalization.

exercise: Try duplicate event IDs, missing devices and null mandatory fields.
interview_questions: How does unique differ from primary key?
Why enforce integrity in the DB?
failure_trap: API validation alone cannot arbitrate concurrent writers.

exercise: Compare WHERE, aggregates and anti-joins with null-containing rows.
interview_questions: Why can NOT IN return nothing?
failure_trap: NULL is not zero and = NULL is not IS NULL.

exercise: Join event tags and device metadata and expose a multiplied SUM.
interview_questions: Why can WHERE change a left join?
How can a join inflate an aggregate?
failure_trap: DISTINCT can conceal a model bug.

exercise: Report warehouses with zero events and separate anomaly counts.
interview_questions: How do HAVING and WHERE differ?
Why does COUNT(*) count an unmatched join row?
failure_trap: Outer placeholders are not actual events.

exercise: Return three latest events per device with ID tie-break.
failure_trap: Global LIMIT is not top-N per group.

exercise: Compare three-row averages with ten-minute occurrence-time windows.
failure_trap: Default frame may not match the intended whole partition.

exercise: Write equivalent CTE and subquery summaries and compare plans.
interview_questions: When use EXISTS instead of JOIN?
failure_trap: CTEs do not inherently improve performance.

exercise: Traverse zones with a cycle and explicit detection or visited-path rule.
failure_trap: Unbounded cyclic recursion can fail to terminate.

exercise: Find missing logical IDs and separately count duplicate effects.
interview_questions: Does EXCEPT detect duplicate processing counts?
failure_trap: Set equality alone does not prove one effect per ID.

exercise: Insert inbox and change a metric, then inject second-statement failure.
interview_questions: What follows an error in a transaction?
failure_trap: Marker and effect must not commit separately.

exercise: Repeat SELECT around another commit at two isolation levels.
interview_questions: Why can Read Committed queries disagree?
failure_trap: MVCC does not mean no locks or anomalies.

exercise: Gate business effects on successful unique inbox insertion.
interview_questions: Why is conflict increment not dedup?
failure_trap: Incrementing on conflict repeats a business effect.

exercise: Repair two stale clients overwriting a shared metric.
failure_trap: Transaction syntax alone does not fix unsafe stale writes.

exercise: Make two processors independently withdraw from a shared on-call pool.
interview_questions: Why can snapshots permit write skew?
What must be retried after serialization failure?
failure_trap: Repeatable Read is not Serializable.

exercise: Acquire A then B and B then A and record abort behavior.
interview_questions: What distinguishes deadlock from long wait?
failure_trap: Infinite retry does not solve contention design.

exercise: Crash a relay before and after publication and reconcile claimed rows.
interview_questions: Does it guarantee FIFO or one publication?
failure_trap: Holding locks through unbounded sends still is not cross-system atomicity.

exercise: Compare selective device lookup with full warehouse reporting.
interview_questions: Why can a sequential scan win?
failure_trap: O(log n) does not determine end-to-end query time.

exercise: Compare device/time/ID and time/device indexes on latest-device queries.
interview_questions: What leads this index and why?
failure_trap: No universal column-order rule substitutes for a query.

exercise: Compare literal and prepared predicates on a partial pending-work index.
interview_questions: When can a partial index be used?
failure_trap: Touching indexed columns alone does not qualify the query.

exercise: Observe heap fetches before and after write churn and vacuum.
interview_questions: Why can index-only scan read heap?
failure_trap: Covering fields do not guarantee zero heap access.

exercise: Explain estimation errors, dominant nodes and cache/disk behavior in one plan.
interview_questions: How do rows and loops combine?
failure_trap: EXPLAIN ANALYZE can actually mutate data.

exercise: Vary relation sizes and inspect join strategy and spill behavior.
failure_trap: Algorithm names alone do not establish efficiency.

exercise: Compare estimates on correlated device/warehouse filters with suitable statistics.
interview_questions: Why can a fresh index still get a bad plan?
failure_trap: Uniform distributions are an assumption to test.

exercise: Use timestamp/ID keyset cursor and compare a deep OFFSET plan.
interview_questions: Does it guarantee a cross-request snapshot?
failure_trap: Timestamp-only cursor can skip ties.

exercise: Keep global inbox identity separate while evaluating time partition retention.
interview_questions: Why does event-ID uniqueness need care?
failure_trap: Time partitioning does not automatically preserve event_id-only global uniqueness.

exercise: Add a required field through compatible staged changes.
interview_questions: When is rollback no longer safe?
failure_trap: Remove/rename only after all consumers migrate.

exercise: Measure dead tuples and maintenance with a long-lived snapshot.
interview_questions: Why does DELETE not shrink files immediately?
failure_trap: Disabling maintenance can accumulate bloat and other risks.

exercise: Run excess tasks and ensure finite pool waits and rollback/close.
failure_trap: Request concurrency is not automatically optimal pool size.

exercise: Bind query values and deny schema changes for application role.
interview_questions: Why split app and migration roles?
failure_trap: Concatenated inputs and superuser service accounts expand risk.

exercise: Report local hourly telemetry across DST and define bucket semantics.
failure_trap: Timezone-naive values do not define a global instant.

exercise: Keep identity/time/device typed while storing validated extensible payload.
interview_questions: Why match index to JSON operator?
failure_trap: Schemaless storage does not eliminate contracts.

exercise: Compare validated row insert and COPY-to-staging throughput.
failure_trap: Raw load throughput is not durable business processing rate.

exercise: Design CDC outbox and retained-WAL alert.
failure_trap: Abandoned slots may retain WAL indefinitely.

exercise: Model accepted/published/applied/quarantined event states.
interview_questions: Can progress be guaranteed during infinite outage?
failure_trap: Eventual success does not prove safe intermediate states.

exercise: Prove repeated attempts yield one guarded committed DB effect under declared assumptions.
interview_questions: Can one effect coexist with repeated execution?
failure_trap: Exactly-once needs an observable effect and failure model.

exercise: Lose a committed API response then retry the same logical request.
failure_trap: New IDs on retries defeat application idempotency.

exercise: Crash after publish acknowledgement but before marking publication.
failure_trap: Outbox relay is not a DB-plus-Kafka atomic transaction.

exercise: Replay an old ID after deleting its marker and demonstrate the broken invariant.
interview_questions: What if payload changes under same ID?
failure_trap: Average retry time ignores manual resets and old outbox rows.

exercise: Process out-of-order device sequences and specify aggregate/latest-state policy.
interview_questions: Does broker order imply increasing source time?
Should old events overwrite latest state?
failure_trap: Wall clocks do not define universal business order.

exercise: Quantify retries across API, relay and consumer.
interview_questions: Why can retry cause cascading failure?
Which operations are safe to retry?
failure_trap: Independent infinite budgets multiply overload.

exercise: Explain why isolated replicas cannot both accept invariant-sensitive writes freely.
interview_questions: Does eventual consistency mean no guarantees?
failure_trap: Choose-any-two slogan omits crucial assumptions.

exercise: Replay same event-time dataset at different arrival speeds.
interview_questions: Can watermark prove completeness under unbounded lateness?
failure_trap: A heuristic watermark is not a universal completeness proof.

exercise: Construct clock-ordered events with no causal relation.
interview_questions: Does smaller Lamport clock prove causality?
failure_trap: Clock order converse is false.

exercise: Measure one queue population and verify mean units and conservation.
interview_questions: Can it describe ever-growing backlog at equilibrium?
failure_trap: p99 is not mean sojourn and offered rate is not always admitted rate.

exercise: Derive backlog=60000 and catch-up=1200s for arrival100/s service150/s outage600s.
interview_questions: What if mu never exceeds lambda?
failure_trap: backlog/mu ignores continuing arrivals.

exercise: Measure serial coordination before increasing process count.
interview_questions: Why can actual speedup be worse?
failure_trap: n workers do not guarantee n throughput.

exercise: Overdrive sink and prove finite resources with explicit outcomes.
interview_questions: Why is unbounded queue delayed failure?
failure_trap: Unbounded sustained admission defeats finite processing capacity.

exercise: Define acceptance availability and accepted-to-effect freshness separately.
failure_trap: Excluding failures manufactures good metrics.

exercise: Record expected invariant and untested boundaries for every fault.
failure_trap: Restart tests do not prove disk/region-loss resilience.

exercise: Pause relay beyond lease and prevent it from marking work reclaimed by another.
failure_trap: Expired workers may continue operating.

exercise: Verify accepted IDs equal disjoint completed/quarantined/pending IDs.
interview_questions: What if loss and duplication cancel?
failure_trap: 100 accepted and 100 rows can conceal both loss and duplicates.

exercise: Design optional sender with explicit provider idempotency boundary.
failure_trap: Local inbox does not protect arbitrary external effects.

exercise: Explain log agreement under leader change and limits of timely progress.
failure_trap: Kafka data ISR is not automatically a generic Raft majority rule.

exercise: Enumerate one-event crash/retry model and turn failures into tests.
interview_questions: Does finite exploration prove unbounded implementation?
What hidden race can abstraction miss?
failure_trap: Bounded checking is not universal implementation correctness.

exercise: Restore business state and markers consistently within allowed replay policy.
failure_trap: Restoring effects without markers can duplicate old effects.

exercise: Save workload, configs, resources and outcomes for repeated runs.
failure_trap: Laptop enqueue peaks are not durable production capacity.

exercise: Distinguish mergeable counters from invariant-sensitive inventory updates.
failure_trap: Every invariant cannot be repaired by arbitrary eventual merge.
